Work / AST-Level Conflict Detection for ServiceNow Customizations
ServiceNow

AST-Level Conflict Detection for ServiceNow Customizations

Enterprise SaaS · Confidential

the challenge

ServiceNow instances accumulate customizations from multiple teams over time, and conflicts between them are notoriously hard to catch before deployment — the client's existing scanner was producing false positives, in some cases flagging and even proposing deletion of valid code, because it lacked origin and taint tracking at the AST level.

our approach

Rather than patch the symptom with more prompt engineering on the AI resolution layer, we traced the root cause to the scanner itself: without AST-level taint tracking, the system couldn't distinguish a legitimate `current.insert()` call from a genuine DOM manipulation risk. We rebuilt the detection logic around proper origin tracking first, then layered the AI resolution system on top of a source of truth it could actually trust.

what we built

A six-layer resolution architecture — source of truth, output verification, provider resilience, a human-review UX with diffs, deployment snapshots, and observability — sitting on top of a corrected Python AST scanner. We also audited and hardened the Node.js backend for security gaps (SSRF exposure, missing auth checks, SSE data leakage, prompt injection vectors) and fixed several correctness bugs, including an allowlist mismatch that was silently discarding valid analyzer output.

the outcome

False positives dropped as the scanner gained the context it was missing, and the human-review layer now gives engineers an auditable diff instead of a black-box suggestion — turning an AI feature that was actively eroding trust into one the team could rely on.
